dependencies.reference: DOM, CSS, PointerEvent and accessibility APIs
dependencies.rationale: Browser controls have no Electron, Node, native handles or direct privileged persistence.
The real window editor composition owns the style scope and lifecycle. Modern UI assembly remains mandatory before visual sign-off.

divergences.summary: Keep original selectors and declarations, adding only a zero-specificity Proctor scope and exact theme variable prefix mapping. Original important declarations remain in reviewed override-layer rules.

Move existing product-specific ButtonControl, ToggleControl and MenuControl into explicitly named files with their unchanged styles/callers. They are not used as substitutes for upstream Button/Toggle/Menu contracts.

Retain the original hover delegation and cached default behavior. Proctor bindings are disposable and store live owner records so teardown in either order never restores a disposed service. Instant delegates remain consumer-owned; shared defaults are window-owned.

Source controls accept disposable constructed stylesheet handles and retain their original selector/state rules under the Proctor namespace and editor scope; ownership replaces HTMLStyleElement mutation under renderer CSP.

verification.obligation: Verify complete source contracts with existing callers and the actual browser dependencies.
Verify pinned complete files and exact nested third-party runtime/notices. Composed UI, control tests and accessibility matrix remain separate completion requirements.

Real sandboxed Electron verification of completion acceptance and undo, diagnostics, computed hover/control geometry, Settings and JSON title icons, both view-switch tooltips, packaged font loading and theme transitions.
Verify nested hover bindings in both teardown orders and that repeatedly disposed source controls alone own their instant hover delegates.
